correctness.rationale: At N=3^k every length-N factor belongs to the zero word or one of the two padded block-edge families; each family is injective by its last or first one. Put L=N/3, so the block is H0^LH. A cross-family equality requires both retained lengths at least 2L since the other family's boundary zeros are at most L. At 2L the only equality is the shared 0^LH0^L. Above 2L, aligning the unique run of L zeros forces both retained lengths to be N. The gaps between ones are 1+3^ν₂(j); the two doubled prefix histograms consequently drop one at weight M/2 and one at M. Each fixed reduced dyadic of denominator 2^r then has limiting mass 3^(−r), and all these masses sum to one, so there is no escape of mass. Conditional uniformity over level r gives variance (1−4^(−(r−1)))/12 and summing with level weights (1/3)(2/3)^(r−1) gives 1/20; symmetry gives mean 1/2.
residual_risks: The bounded census is not an all-k proof. The analytic block and probability arguments concern uniformly sampled distinct factors, not random starting positions.
